name: Rasgulla
subtitle: Chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy

ingredients.note: not UHT — it will not curdle cleanly
omit to keep it gluten-free; handle the balls gently

prepNotes: Everything depends on the chhena: drained enough to hold, moist enough to knead smooth. Squeeze it dry and the rasgulla turns rubbery.
The syrup must be thin. A thick syrup cannot penetrate the dumpling and it stays raw in the middle.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil, take it off the heat, and add lemon juice a little at a time until the curds separate cleanly from greenish whey.
Strain through muslin and rinse under cold water to wash out the acid. Hang 30 minutes — no longer.
steps.tip: Rinsing matters; unrinsed chhena tastes of lemon.

steps.text: Knead the chhena on a plate with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes, until it goes from grainy to smooth and slightly greasy. Work in the maida if using.
steps.tip: This is the step people cut short, and it is why rasgullas crack.

steps.text: Roll into 12 crack-free balls, smaller than you want them finished — they double.
Bring the sugar and water to a rolling boil with the cardamom. Slide the balls in, cover, and boil hard for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Hard boil, lid on. A gentle simmer will not inflate them.

steps.text: Cool in the syrup, add rose water, and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated in its syrup, and the texture is best from the second day. Do not freeze.
